editorial: We visited in September, which perhaps wasn’t the best time to visit the Yucatan peninsula. The wet season (June to October) in Yucatan tends to be HOT and HUMID as we found out for ourselves. Luckily, we weren’t caught up in a hurricane!

Home to Chichen-itza and Bacalar, as well as Cancun and Tulum, Yucatan is best visited during the dry season (December to April) when the weather is pleasant and the seas are calm. One word of caution… a lot of Mexico’s norther neighbours descend on its beaches during spring break in March.
Mexico City, which is inland and at an altitude, follows the four seasons format and had pleasant fall-like weather in September, so no complaints there.
